articles.title: Kansas revoked 1,700 transgender drivers’ licenses. Some are leaving the state.
articles.summary: Kansas is one of five states to prohibit trans people from changing gender markers on ID and the first to pass a law that retroactively cancels licenses.
articles.body: Some 1,700 Kansans had their driver’s licenses invalidated last month. It wasn’t for racking up speeding tickets or a DUI charge, but because they are transgender. Kansas is one of five states to prohibit trans people from changing the gender marker on their licenses, but it is the first to pass a law that retroactively cancels licenses that were already changed. The law also invalidated birth certificates for those who updated their gender markers. Hundreds of trans drivers already received letters from the state informing them their documents were “invalid immediately” and they “may be subject to additional penalties” if they continue to drive, unless they surrender the license to the Kansas Division of Vehicles and receive a new one with their birth sex. “I’m pretty heartbroken,” said Jaelynn Abegg, a 41-year-old trans woman living in Wichita who received a letter. She said she will not turn in her license and plans to move this month to another state. “It is a continuation of the message that the Legislature has been sending out for years now, and that is that transgender people are not welcome in Kansas,” she said. Two anonymous trans residents sued Kansas last month, arguing that the law violates state protections for personal autonomy, privacy, equality, due process and freedom of speech. On Tuesday, Douglas County District Judge James McCabria declined to grant a temporary restraining order against the law while the case proceeds. McCabria wrote in his decision that there isn't enough evidence to show that trans people will face harassment and discrimination if they have to use bathrooms or show IDs that conflict with their gender identities. Kansas law was years in the making Kansas had allowed trans people to update the gender markers on their IDs since 2007. Then in 2023, it changed its legal definition of sex to be male or female and assigned at birth. Fifteen other states have made a similar change in the past few years — and President Donald Trump issued an executive order declaring that there are only two unchangeable sexes. The State Department now prohibits trans people from changing the gender markers on their passports. Kansas Attorney General Kris Kobach sued the state, arguing that allowing people to update their gender markers violated the 2023 law. Last year, the Kansas Supreme Court affirmed an appeals court decision and allowed gender marker changes to resume. In January, Kobach backed the new bill he said would “correct an error” by the courts. The state Senate added a provision prohibiting trans people from using bathrooms that align with their gender identities in government-owned buildings. It was passed without public comment. The penalties for violating the provision can be $1,000 for individuals and up to $125,000 for government entities with more than one infraction. Last month, Democratic Gov. Laura Kelly vetoed the bill, saying the Legislature “should stay out of the business of telling Kansans how to go to the bathroom and instead stay focused on how to make life more affordable for Kansans.” Days later, the Republican-held state Legislature overrode her veto. Kansas House Speaker Daniel Hawkins, a Republican, said in a statement at the time that the law’s purpose was to protect women. “This isn’t about scoring political points, but doing what’s right for women and girls across our communities,” he said, according to the Kansas Reflector. Hawkins did not respond to NBC News’ request for comment. State Rep. Mark Schreiber, the only Republican to vote against the bill, told NBC News he agreed with the appeals court that Kobach could not show how allowing trans people to change the gender markers on their licenses caused harm to the state. “I don’t have any trans folks in my family, but I know trans people,” he said, adding that they aren’t looking for special privileges and just want to live their lives. “And we seem to keep passing laws that keep getting in the way of that.” Harper Seldin, one of the ACLU attorneys involved in the lawsuit, said during court arguments Friday that the Kansas Legislature singled out trans Kansans "for unique social stigma." "They were suddenly required, with no notice or opportunity to be heard, to present themselves to the DMV to obtain driver's licenses that announced to everyone — the teller at the bank, the clerk at the hotel, the poll worker on election day — that they are transgender," Seldin said. Trans people have long reported facing more harassment and discrimination while using IDs that don't align with their gender identity or expression, and many trans Kansans said they fear that their daily risk of facing such harassment would only increase as a result of the law. ‘There was no plan whatsoever’ Over the last five years, dozens of states have considered bills targeting transgender people, but the majority of those have targeted people’s ability to play on school sports teams that align with their gender identities and minors’ access to transition-related care. In the last few years, state and federal policies have shifted to focus on changing legal definitions of sex and restricting access to updated identity documents. Logan Casey, director of policy research at the Movement Advancement Project, an LGBTQ think tank that tracks legislation, described these broader laws as “gender regulation laws” that attack the fundamental rights and identity of trans people. “The point all along for the people pushing these bills and these attacks has been to single out transgender people and create a license to discriminate against transgender people and remove them from public life,” he said. “In effect, trying to get them to stop being transgender.” Kansas’ law took effect immediately after it was published in the register Feb. 26. A spokesperson for the Kansas Department of Revenue told the Kansas Reflector that the law invalidated about 1,700 licenses. The department did not respond to a request for comment. During the court hearing Friday, Kobach said the department had so far sent letters to 275 Kansans and 138 had received new licenses. Andrea Ellis, a 34-year-old trans woman living in Wellington, said she received a letter Wednesday even though she never changed the gender marker on her license — she only legally changed her name on it in December. She drove to the DMV the next day, where she said staff were confused about what to do and said her license had a “flag” on it. They cut the corner off her license and gave her a temporary one. But later that day, they called her and said she had to return to the DMV because they made an error. When she went back, she said they gave her another temporary license that looked the same as the first. “They claim that it was thought out, and everything else, but there was no grace period unlike any other kind of rollout program,” Ellis said. “There was no plan whatsoever.” Some trans residents, like Matthew Neumann, said they still haven’t received any notification regarding their licenses. Neumann, who is the executive director of the LGBTQ Foundation of Kansas, said he’s been checking the validity of his license every day on the Kansas Department of Revenue website, and it’s still valid as of Friday. Neumann said his organization has raised funds to help trans Kansans pay to update their licenses. Getting a license with an updated gender marker costs $8.75, while receiving a new ID is $26. Neumann has lived in Larned, Kansas, for 20 years and said he will never leave. He said he’s been threatened over his restroom use, and he fears he could face more harassment under the new law. “I’m just disappointed and frustrated,” he said. “I’m just hoping that maybe this is the wake up call we need,” he said.

articles.title: Chilling grin of man accused of killing cop’s wife, daughter outside court after he gets 10 yrs in jail
articles.summary: Raipur: Kuldeep Sahu grins outside Surajpur court after getting 10 years for attempt to murder; convicted in 2024 cop’s wife-daughter murder, sentencing Oct 8.
articles.body: Raipur: “Achchha wala dikhaiyega, smile karte hue (Use a good pic, smiling one).” Moments after a Surajpur district fast-track court sentenced him to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment for trying to mow down policemen with a car, Kuldeep Sahu, 28, walked out smiling at cameras and asked mediapersons to use his smiling picture.The video of Sahu grinning outside the courtroom circulated widely on social media, drawing attention not just to Monday’s sentence but also to the far graver case awaiting its final order: the 2024 murder of a head constable’s wife and minor daughter, in which Sahu and three others have been convicted. The court will pronounce the quantum of sentence in that case on Oct 8.Sahu was brought from Ambikapur central jail to Surajpur court under heavy security.The 10-year sentence relates to an incident from the night of Oct 13, 2024, when police were searching for Sahu after he attacked constable Ghanshyam Sonwani at Surajpur’s old bus stand by throwing boiling oil on him. During the ensuing police action, Sahu tried to run over a policeman with a car, according to the prosecution.The fast-track court convicted him in the attempt-to-murder case and sentenced him to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment. Five other accused in that case were acquitted.The same night, the wife and minor daughter of a head constable posted in Surajpur were killed inside their rented house. Their bodies were later found around 5 km away.In that case, the court convicted Sahu along with Rinku alias Phool Singh, Chandrakant Chaudhary and Aryan Vishwakarma on charges including murder. Two other accused were acquitted. The court has reserved Oct 8 for sentencing.The prosecution case also includes sexual assault and Pocso Act charges linked to the double murder.Sahu had separately faced allegations of firing at a police team led by the then Bishrampur police station in-charge while fleeing near Latori, but he and another accused were acquitted in that case for lack of sufficient evidence.The double murder had triggered widespread outrage in Surajpur, with residents taking to the streets demanding strict punishment. Vehicles parked outside Sahu’s house and godown were torched during the unrest.Police records showed that Sahu had figured in more than two dozen criminal cases before the murders. articles.title: Jamia Millia Islamia suspends PhD scholar for 5 days over protest against hostel evictions
articles.summary: Jamia Millia Islamia suspends a PhD scholar for 5 days over alleged role in protest against women hostellers’ eviction notices; university cites rules.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Jamia Millia Islamia has suspended a PhD scholar for five days for allegedly participating in a protest gathering on Monday against the alleged “retaliatory” eviction notices served to several women hostellers who had staged a prolonged agitation over bugs found in mess food. The scholar has been barred from entering the campus during the suspension period.The show-cause notice, issued by the office of the chief proctor on Sept 28, said an unauthorised gathering was held at the central canteen at 5pm that day, disrupting the university’s routine functioning and affecting teaching, learning and research activities in nearby departments, laboratories and libraries. It accused the scholar of delivering a speech and “giving publicity to misleading accounts and rumours”, thereby inciting other students to breach discipline.The notice said his actions amounted to “gross misconduct” under various clauses of the university’s students’ discipline ordinance. He has been directed to explain by Oct 5 why a higher punishment should not be imposed.Speaking to TOI, the student said the protest was organised by women hostel residents against a recent alleged forced eviction, which they believed was retaliatory following their protests over food safety in the mess.Earlier, hostellers had alleged eviction notices were served on them for participating in protests against the mess food. The administration, however, had said the students did not meet the eligibility criteria and that hostel renewal was carried out every year on the basis of merit.Saima Saeed, chief public relations officer, Jamia Millia Islamia, said the university is not stopping anyone from exercising their right to protest. “The university has a designated site for protests, as per court orders, and if anyone violates these guidelines and disrupts the academic environment, the university is bound to take action. Secondly, Jamia follows a merit-based hostel allocation system. If a student does not meet the prescribed 55% marks criterion, we are only following the established procedure. articles.title: Military-grade drones worth Rs 1 crore seized at Delhi airport
articles.summary: Customs at Delhi IGI Airport seized professional-grade drones and parts worth Rs 1 crore from three passengers arriving from Hong Kong via Vietnam; DGCA registration required.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Three Indian passengers have been charged for attempting to smuggle drones and their parts worth Rs 1 crore. These passengers had arrived at IGI Airport on Sept 25 from Hong Kong via Vietnam.During Customs proceedings, the passengers were subjected to a baggage search, which resulted in the recovery of 10 autel robotics mdx-1 drones, 11 remote controllers of autel robotics mdx-1 drones, 10 adaptors, 10 USB chargers, 20 data cables, 40 remote controller joysticks and other parts. They also recovered one iPhone 18 Pro Max 512 GB.“Chartered engineer informed Customs officers that these are professional-grade drones with thermal imaging and laser range-finder and are military/defence grade UAV. They also require mandatory DGCA registration for each drone. The total market value was assessed at Rs 1 crore,” said a Customs official.The passengers told officials that the drones and their parts were brought from Hong Kong for a friend who owns them.“One passenger also stated that he intentionally smuggled these drones into India without declaration to the Customs authorities and without payment of applicable Customs duty,” said the official.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: ‘UP is my karmabhoomi, state will be starting point of my political journey’: Ex-IAS Divya Mittal
articles.summary: Ex-IAS officer Divya Mittal, 2013 UP cadre, enters politics independently in Uttar Pradesh, vows citizen-led platform, flags rural issues, road safety and jobs.
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal on Tuesday announced her entry into politics but said she won’t join any party. Uttar Pradesh is my “karmabhoomi” and the state would be the starting point of my political journey, she said.Mittal, a 2013 batch UP cadre officer, resigned from the service earlier this month. Mittal said she would work directly with citizens and build an independent platform.She alleged that rumours circulated after her resignation were intended to discourage newcomers from entering public life. “I will not be deterred from raising public issues,” she said.In a video statement, Mittal said her administrative experience drove her decision. “I realised that many problems of the public do not get resolved even when approvals, funds and provisions are in place,” she said, adding, “There are people whose voices do not reach govt, and even when they do, their problems remain unheard.”“I want politics of intent, justice, concern and long-term thinking,” she said. “My objective is not just to replace political leaders. It is to change the way politics functions,” she added.She cited the example of a remote village where residents had sought a school offering education beyond Class V. Mittal said she approved the proposal, but construction had not begun years later. “It was not a question of funds or rules. There was a lack of intent,” she said.She also referred to a landless beneficiary who had official documents for an allotted plot but did not get its physical possession. “Inquiries found irregularities in the reports, and corrective action was taken. Yet the work did not move forward,” Mittal said, questioning what she described as “higher-level interference” in cases where people were legally entitled to relief.Mittal said she wanted to take up issues, including poor rural infrastructure, unsafe roads, examination paper leaks and employment concerns in the age of artificial intelligence. These, she said, needed greater public debate and attention from policymakers.She appealed to people from different walks of life, including teachers, farmers, students, doctors, labourers and lawyers, to join her effort. “Meaningful political change can come only through collective public participation,” she said.During her 13-year career, she also served as the district magistrate of Mirzapur and Deoria.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: Gulzar Singh case: Complainant has no video of father’s death, cops tell Punjab and Haryana high court
articles.summary: Punjab govt tells Punjab and Haryana HC Gulzar Singh’s family hasn’t handed over the original suicide video/device; police rely on social media clips as SIT probes case.
articles.body: CHANDIGARH: Punjab govt has told the Punjab and Haryana high court that despite repeated efforts, the original video/device on which alleged suicide victim Gulzar Singh’s purported video was recorded has not been handed over to the police by the complainant or his family members.In its status report filed before the division bench of Chief Justice Ashwini Kumar and Justice Rohit Kapoor, the state govt said efforts were made to bring on record the original video/device, but the complainant and the family members of Gulzar Singh did not submit them.The report states that notices under Section 94 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were issued to complainant Lakhwinder Singh, who is Gulzar’s son, on Sept 15, 17, 20 and 27 for the production of the device. The report stated that Lakhwinder, in his statement on Sept 27, stated that he did not have any video regarding the death of his father.The SIT, however, said multiple videos had been collected as part of the investigation through social-media monitoring. “The said videos have been obtained through social monitoring vide DDR No. 45 dated September 26, 2026,” the report states.It states that the videos are being analysed as “there are multiple videos with different versions”.According to the status report, in one of the videos, Gulzar Singh is heard naming Raj Sarpanch, Vicky, Sukha Conductor and Gona, who are accused in the present FIR. The report states that “his statement in the said video corroborates with the statement given by complainant Lakhwinder Singh”.The report also states that in another video, Gulzar can be seen asking questions regarding the incident and its details.The police said notices were also issued under Section 94 of the BNSS to media channels, calling upon them to provide the original video recordings along with requisite certificates under Section 63(4)(c) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, “for the purpose of establishing their authenticity”.The status report has been filed by Sangrur senior superintendent of police Dr Rajvot Grewal, a member of the special investigation team that is probing the suicide case, in compliance with the high court’s Sept 16 order.The report states that FIR No. 204 dated Sept 8 was registered at Dirba police station under Section 108 of the BNS and sections 3(1)(r) and 3(1)(s) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act against five persons — Baljit Singh alias Raj, Sukhdev Singh alias Sukha Conductor, Vicky Singh alias Vicky Member, Gona Singh and Baljinder Kaur.It states that Baljit, Vicky, Gona and Baljinder were arrested on Sept 8 and remanded in judicial custody. Sukhdev, however, “is absconding as on today”.Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old agricultural laborer from Toor Banjara village in Punjab’s Sangrur district, died by suicide on Sept 7, after consuming poison following a public confrontation with Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema over the local drug menace on Sept 6.The SIT said a look-out circular was issued against Sukhdev, besides a message to all SHOs in Punjab, a public notice and letters to the Regional Transport Authority, Lead Bank, Sangrur, and Bureau of Immigration to trace him and gather information about his vehicle, financial transactions and travel history. articles.title: Voo da Flydubai é desviado após briga física entre pilotos | G1
articles.standfirst: Voo FZ1073 da Flydubai, que ia de Dubai a Tel Aviv, desviou sua rota rumo à Arábia Saudita após emitir sinais de emergência. Pilotos tiveram confronto físico e foram hospitalizados após aterrissagem, segundo a Reuters e autoridades sauditas.
articles.summary: O voo da Flydubai para Israel foi desviado após briga física entre pilotos com relatos de esfaqueamento, motivando investigação por suspeita de terrorismo.
articles.body:
Imagens feitas a partir do Flightradar24 mostram a rota do voo que partiu de Dubai , nos Emirados Árabes Unidos, com destino a Tel Aviv , em Israel , e que foi desviado para a Arábia Saudita após uma briga entre pilotos nesta quarta-feira (30).

O voo FZ1073, da Flydubai, mudou de rota enquanto sobrevoava o espaço aéreo da Jordânia. A aeronave emitiu inicialmente o código 7700, que indica uma emergência geral, e, alguns minutos depois, acionou o código 7500, usado para indicar uma possível interferência ilegal.

O Boeing 737 voltou a emitir o código de emergência geral antes de pousar no aeroporto de Tabuk, no noroeste da Arábia Saudita, segundo o site.

O governo Netanyahu afirmou suspeitar de uma tentativa de "ataque terrorista".

Os sinais de emergência foram emitidos após os pilotos entrarem em uma briga que incluiu confronto físico, e Israel acredita que pode ter se tratado de uma tentativa de "ataque terrorista" , disseram autoridades do governo israelense à Reuters.

O ministro da Segurança Nacional israelense, Itamar Ben Gvir, afirmou que "um terrorista planejou derrubar um avião e assassinar os 180 israelenses a bordo". Horas antes, o gabinete do premiê Benjamin Netanyahu tinha dito acreditar que não se tratava de uma tentativa de sequestro e estava "tudo sob controle".

Segundo relatos, havia uma faca a bordo e um dos pilotos teria sido esfaqueado pelo outro, com "sangue por todo o lado" e pânico entre os passageiros. Leia mais abaixo.

Passageiros ensanguentados após briga entre pilotos em voo da Flydubai rumo a Israel que foi desviado para a Arábia Saudita em 30 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Reprodução/redes sociais

O aeroporto saudita de Tabuk, onde o voo aterrissou, afirmou que tanto o piloto quanto o copiloto ficaram feridos e foram hospitalizados , e que passageiros também receberam atendimento.

O incidente provocou uma grande operação de segurança em Israel, que não mantém relações diplomáticas oficiais com a Arábia Saudita, onde o avião pousou. Netanyahu realizou consultas sobre o caso e seu gabinete afirmou que todos os esforços estavam sendo feitos para levar os passageiros israelenses de volta a Israel.

Havia ao menos 150 passageiros israelenses a bordo, segundo a mídia de Israel. A Flydubai opera voos diários entre Dubai e Tel Aviv, uma rota popular entre cidadãos israelenses.

Voo FZ1073 da Flydubai com destino a Tel Aviv desvia rota após incidente a bordo em 30 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Flightradar24.com/Handout via REUTERS

O voo aterrissou às 3h45 no horário de Brasília no aeroporto de Tabuk, no noroeste da Arábia Saudita, e todos os passageiros estavam seguros, segundo a Flydubai e a concessionária saudita que administra o local.

Os dados de voo indicaram que a aeronave desceu de forma repentina e rápida e despencou 4,3 mil metros em cerca de 30 segundos pouco antes do primeiro sinal de emergência ser emitido, informou o Flightradar24.

A mídia israelense afirmou que o Mossad, a principal agência de inteligência do país e responsável por operações especiais e secretas, está investigando o incidente.

Um porta-voz da companhia aérea disse apenas que houve um "incidente" durante o voo, o que fez com que fosse desviado para Tabuk, onde pousou em segurança.

Horas depois, um segundo voo da Flydubai rumo a Tel Aviv fez um breve desvio em sua rota, segundo o FlightRadar24, porém seguia o caminho até a última atualização desta reportagem.

A mãe de uma passageira que estava a bordo do voo disse à agência Reuters que a filha lhe contou ter ouvido gritos e que um homem pegou uma faca, colocou o piloto no chão e que havia sangue por toda parte.

"Ela me ligou [após aterrissar] e disse que eles ouviram vozes, alguém pediu ajuda. Era o piloto. Ele estava gritando: ‘Ajuda, ajuda, ajuda!’. O avião começou a perder o controle, então todas as pessoas começaram a gritar e acharam que iriam morrer", disse Yasmin Abu Kasis, com base no relato da filha Miriam.

"Depois de alguns minutos, outros dois pilotos assumiram o controle. Alguns israelenses correram até um homem, e nesse momento ele pegou uma faca e tentou matar o piloto. Eles seguraram a mão dele e o colocaram no chão. Havia muito sangue por toda parte ”, completou Yasmin.

Ainda segundo Yasmin, os passageiros ficaram "estressados e em choque" com toda a situação.

Uma outra passageira afirmou à agência AFP que o piloto tentou matar o copiloto.

articles.title: Voo para Israel é desviado após ataque entre pilotos: o que se sabe  | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo autoridades israelenses, copiloto atacou piloto e fez aeronave despencar 4,3 mil metros no ar. Com ajuda de pilotos 'reserva', a aeronave conseguiu pousar em segurança na Arábia Saudita.
articles.summary: Voo da Flydubai com destino a Tel Aviv foi desviado para a Arábia Saudita após confronto entre pilotos. Veja o que se sabe e o que falta esclarecer.
articles.body:
Um voo da FlyDubai com destino a Israel foi desviado para a Arábia Saudita nesta quarta-feira (30) depois que o copiloto atacou o piloto com uma faca durante a viagem, segundo autoridades israelenses.

O governo de Israel trata o caso como uma tentativa de ataque terrorista. As circunstâncias, porém, ainda estão sendo investigadas.

Veja abaixo o que já se sabe e o que ainda não foi esclarecido:

O avião que transportava passageiros que estavam no voo da Flydubai com destino a Israel, saído dos Emirados Árabes Unidos e desviado para a Arábia Saudita após emitir um sinal de emergência, chega ao Aeroporto Internacional Ben Gurion, em Lod, perto de Tel Aviv, Israel. — Foto: Ammar Awad / Reuters

O voo FZ1073 saiu de Dubai, nos Emirados Árabes Unidos, e tinha como destino o aeroporto Ben Gurion, em Tel Aviv , Israel.

A FlyDubai opera voos regulares entre as duas cidades. A rota é usada com frequência por passageiros israelenses que viajam para Dubai.

O Boeing 737 tinha 180 passageiros, segundo autoridades israelenses. O ministro da Segurança Nacional de Israel, Itamar Ben Gvir, afirmou que 100 passageiros eram israelenses.

Outros relatos da imprensa israelense apontaram que pelo menos 150 passageiros eram do país. A companhia aérea informou que todos estavam em segurança depois do pouso.

O confronto ocorreu quando o avião já estava próximo de Israel e sobrevoava a Jordânia . Segundo autoridades israelenses , o copiloto atacou o piloto com uma faca. Os dois entraram em confronto físico.

O embate teria deixado os dois pilotos feridos e fez com que a aeronave perdesse o controle temporariamente. Passageiros relataram ter ouvido gritos e pedidos de ajuda vindos da cabine de comando.

A mãe de uma passageira contou à Reuters que a filha ouviu um dos pilotos gritar por ajuda.

A sequência exata de fatos a bordo entre o confronto entre os pilotos e o pouso ainda não havia sido totalmente esclarecida até o momento, porém um porta-voz de Netanyahu disse à Reuters que o piloto, mesmo ferido, coberto de sangue e caído no chão, conseguiu acionar a abertura da porta da cabine de comando.

O que houve com o avião durante o ataque?

O avião chegou a despencar no ar. Dados do site de monitoramento Flightradar24 indicam que a aeronave perdeu aproximadamente 4.300 metros de altitude em cerca de 30 segundos .

A aeronave estava sobrevoando a Jordânia quando começou a emitir sinais de emergência. A queda brusca ocorreu pouco antes do primeiro alerta.

Quais sinais de emergência foram emitidos?

O avião transmitiu diferentes códigos de emergência durante o incidente. Primeiro, foi acionado o código 7700, usado para indicar uma emergência geral.

Pouco depois, a aeronave transmitiu o código 7500, usado na aviação para indicar uma possível interferência ilegal, como um sequestro ou outra situação de tomada de controle.

O código de emergência geral voltou a ser emitido posteriormente.

Por que o avião foi para a Arábia Saudita?

Depois dos sinais de emergência, a aeronave mudou de rota e seguiu para Tabuk, no noroeste da Arábia Saudita.

O aeroporto da cidade confirmou que o pousou aconteceu em segurança.

O piloto e o copiloto foram hospitalizados. Passageiros também receberam atendimento médico.

Um porta-voz do primeiro-ministro israelense, Benjamin Netanyahu , disse à Reuters que outros pilotos que estavam entre os passageiros assumiram o controle do avião e ajudaram no pouso.

Um segundo par de pilotos da FlyDubai estava a bordo do avião porque assumiria o cockipit quando o avião pousasse em Israel. Diante do incidente, a dupla assumiu o controle da aeronave e pousou em segurança na Arábia Saudita.

As identidades dos pilotos 'reserva' não haviam sido reveladas até a última atualização desta reportagem.

A FlyDubai não entrou em tantos detalhes em seu comunicado oficial, e afirmou apenas que "a aeronave foi controlada com sucesso pela tripulação que estava na ativa e viajava no voo, que desviou a rota e pousou a aeronave em segurança no Aeroporto de Tabuk (TUU)".

Familiares e pessoas próximas dos passageiros do voo da Flydubai — Foto: Michal Yaakov Itzhaki / Reuters

Ainda não há uma explicação oficial sobre o motivo pelo qual o copiloto teria atacado o comandante.

Autoridades israelenses afirmam que o episódio foi uma tentativa de ataque terrorista e que o objetivo era matar os passageiros israelenses. Em depoimento, o autor do atentado afirmou que não é ligado a nenhum grupo jihadista e que agiu por conta própria .

O governo israelense, porém, ainda não apresentou publicamente uma explicação detalhada sobre a motivação do homem.

A investigação deve buscar esclarecer se houve motivação política ou religiosa, um conflito pessoal entre os pilotos ou outro motivo.

Como o copiloto entrou com uma faca no avião?

Ainda não foi explicado como a faca teria sido levada para dentro da aeronave. A informação sobre a presença da arma aparece em relatos de passageiros e em declarações de autoridades israelenses .

Não foi divulgado até o momento se a faca pertencia ao copiloto ou se estava disponível em alguma área do avião.

A sequência exata do confronto ainda não foi esclarecida. Relatos indicam que houve uma discussão e um confronto físico entre os dois pilotos dentro da cabine de comando.

Segundo autoridades israelenses, o copiloto atacou o piloto com uma faca.

Não há confirmação de que algum passageiro tenha sido ferido diretamente pelo ataque com a faca. A FlyDubai informou que a lgumas das pessoas a bordo receberam atendimento médico depois do pouso.

Ainda não foi divulgado um balanço detalhado sobre o número de pessoas machucadas e a gravidade dos ferimentos.

O piloto e o copiloto ficaram feridos e foram levados a um hospital em Tabuk.

Uma mulher carrega um cachorro enquanto passageiros que estavam no voo da Flydubai com destino a Israel, saído dos Emirados Árabes Unidos e desviado para a Arábia Saudita após emitir um sinal de emergência. — Foto: Ammar Awad / Reuters

articles.title: WhatsApp: como ativar o controle parental para adolescentes | G1
articles.standfirst: Pais e responsáveis podem definir quem pode adicionar o adolescente a grupos, receber notificações sobre algumas atividades e escolher como ele usa canais e atualizações de status.
articles.summary: Pais e responsáveis podem definir quem pode adicionar o adolescente a grupos, receber notificações sobre algumas atividades e escolher como ele usa canais e atualizações de status.
articles.body:
O WhatsApp anunciou nesta quarta-feira (30) novos controles parentais para adolescentes no Brasil. Segundo a empresa, pais e responsáveis poderão definir como menores de idade usam o aplicativo de mensagens. As novidades já estão disponíveis para todos a partir de hoje. (Veja abaixo como habilitar.)

As novidades dão continuidade a uma atualização feita pela Meta em março, quando foram liberadas ferramentas semelhantes de proteção para menores de 13 anos no WhatsApp. Agora, os controles também passam a atender adolescentes.

A configuração precisa ser feita primeiro no celular do adolescente e depois vinculada ao aparelho do pai, mãe ou responsável.

Toque em “Concordar e continuar” e, depois, em “Mais opções” .

Selecione “Criar uma conta gerenciada por pai, mãe ou responsável” .

Cadastre e confirme o número de telefone do adolescente.

Informe a data de nascimento e confirme a idade.

Toque em “Continuar” para iniciar a conexão com a conta do responsável.

Use a câmera do celular para escanear o QR Code exibido no aparelho do adolescente e toque no link que aparecer.

Abra o WhatsApp, toque em “Concordar e continuar” e confirme que você é adulto.

Crie um PIN de seis dígitos. Ele será usado para acessar e alterar as configurações de privacidade da conta.

Toque em “OK” e conclua a configuração no celular do adolescente.

No celular do responsável, acesse “Configurações” e, depois, “Controle parental” para consultar as opções de acompanhamento disponíveis para a conta do adolescente.

WhatsApp logo — Foto: Dimitri Karastelev/Unsplash

Com os novos recursos, pais e responsáveis podem definir quem pode ver a foto de perfil do adolescente e quem pode adicioná-lo a grupos. Eles também podem receber notificações quando o adolescente entrar ou sair de um grupo e quando um grupo do qual ele participa aumentar de número de integrantes.

Também é possível saber com quem o adolescente está conversando, escolher como ele pode usar os canais e definir quais atualizações de status ele pode ver e quem pode visualizar as publicações dele.

A empresa afirma que as ligações feitas e as mensagens enviadas pelo adolescente continuam privadas. Isso significa que os responsáveis não poderão ler as conversas nem receber um relatório sobre com quem o adolescente falou ou para quem ligou .

"Ninguém mais pode ler ou ouvir o conteúdo dessas conversas, nem mesmo o WhatsApp", diz a companhia.

A chegada das funcionalidades ocorre em um momento de pressão no Brasil com o ECA Digital, para garantir um ambiente online seguro para crianças. Essa pressão também ocorre em outros países.

articles.title: Meet Tejas: The rare blue-eyed white tiger who travelled 550 km from Gwalior to become Dehradun Zoo’s newest attraction; "The energetic young tiger immediately started exploring"
articles.summary: Dehradun Zoo just added a new attraction in the form of Tejas, a two-and-a-half-year-old white tiger.
articles.body: Dehradun Zoo just added a new attraction in the form of Tejas, a two-and-a-half-year-old white tiger. It gives wildlife enthusiasts another reason to visit the capital city. The little cub travelled nearly 550 km from Gwalior. He comes following an animal-exchange programme that saw the zoo’s approximately five-year-old Royal Bengal tiger, Bhola, move to Gwalior Zoological Park.For travellers planning a Dehradun visit, however, there is an important catch: Tejas will not be immediately visible to the public. After his journey of more than 14 hours, the young tiger has entered a period of quarantine and observation for about 20 days. So visitors will likely have to wait a month before he is put on display. During this period, his health, behaviour, feeding and adjustment to the new enclosure will be monitored.The blue-eyed Tejas As per reports, Tejas is particularly striking because of his white coat and dark stripes. He has beautiful blue eyes. But despite the unusual appearance, a white tiger is not a separate species or breed of tiger. The white coat results from an inherited colour variation; unlike an albino.As per TOI reports, Tejas was translocated under the administrative supervision of Neena Grewal, principal chief conservator of forests and chief wildlife warden. The transfer was overseen by Vaibhav Singh, divisional forest officer, Dehradun, with a 13-member specialised veterinary team accompanying the tiger. The team was led by Pradeep Mishra, senior veterinarian at Doon Zoo, along with SDO Abhishek Maithani.Sharing his observations on Tejas on the second day after his arrival, Mishra said, “With its white coat, crisp dark stripes and vivid blue eyes, he scanned everything in sight. He didn’t hesitate for a second; the energetic young tiger immediately started exploring, confidently strutting along the fence, sniffing the air and checking out every inch of his new home with bold curiosity.”Dehradun Zoo, a new stop for wildlife loversDehradun Zoo, formerly known as Malsi Deer Park, is located along Mussoorie Road at the foothills of the Shivalik range. The municipal administration describes it as a mini-zoological park developed with objectives that include ex-situ conservation, biodiversity conservation, wildlife education and rescue.The zoo is around 9–10 km from Dehradun's Clock Tower/city centre and lies on the route towards Mussoorie.The addition of Tejas also adds another layer to a city that already works as a gateway to several of Uttarakhand's best-known natural and hill destinations. The state tourism department describes Dehradun as a gateway to Mussoorie, Haridwar and Rishikesh, while also highlighting attractions such as the Forest Research Institute, Sahastradhara, Mindrolling Monastery and zoo.Other wildlife attractions nearbyTravellers interested in seeing wildlife in a natural setting can extend their trip to Rajaji National Park and Tiger Reserve, which spans parts of Dehradun, Haridwar and Pauri Garhwal districts. The reserve is known for its forest landscape and populations of elephants, tigers and leopards, besides a wide variety of birds and other wildlife.Rajaji can therefore complement a Dehradun itinerary for travellers who want to experience both wildlife conservation in a zoo setting and the biodiversity of a protected forest landscape.When should you plan a Dehradun wildlife trip?For those specifically hoping to see Tejas, it is worth waiting until the zoo officially announces that his quarantine period is over and that he is on public display. Travellers should check the latest zoo information.More than just a tiger sightingThe arrival of Tejas gives travellers another reason to revisit Dehradun, but the bigger story is the city's growing appeal as a base for nature, wildlife and outdoor experiences. From the Shivalik foothills and forested landscapes to nearby Rajaji and the road towards Mussoorie, Dehradun offers several ways to build a wildlife-and-nature-focused holiday.And once Tejas completes his quarantine, visitors may have an unusual opportunity: a white tiger in one enclosure and a more traditionally coloured Royal Bengal tiger nearby, offering a striking visual reminder of the natural variation found within the tiger species.You use AI every day. articles.title: Mercedes-Benz GLC EV India launch on this date: Details
articles.summary: Mercedes-Benz will launch the GLC Electric in India on November 4, 2026.
articles.body: Mercedes-Benz will launch the GLC Electric in India on November 4, 2026. The SUV will be assembled at the company’s Chakan plant in Pune and will arrive in the 400 4Matic version. Bookings are expected to open in October. Mercedes-Benz says the Indian launch will come just six months after the model went on sale in Europe, making it the fastest global model from the brand to be locally assembled in India.The GLC Electric 400 4Matic uses a 94kWh battery and has a claimed WLTP range of up to 715km. Its two electric motors power all four wheels and produce 490hp and 800Nm. Mercedes-Benz claims a 0-100kph time of 4.3 seconds, despite the SUV weighing around 2.5 tonnes.The electric SUV supports DC charging at up to 330kW. The company claims a 10-minute charge can add enough energy for up to 300km of range. The international-specification model also gets air suspension and rear-wheel steering with up to 4.5 degrees of steering angle.The GLC Electric gets a wide front grille with illuminated elements, projector LED headlights and star-shaped LED daytime running lights. Its design also includes flush door handles, wheel-arch cladding and alloy wheels of up to 21 inches.At the rear, the SUV gets star-shaped LED tail-lights with circular outlines, connected by a gloss-black strip. The front Mercedes logo is illuminated, while the rear gets a solid 3D badge. Internationally, the 400 4Matic can also be specified with an AMG Line package, which adds a different grille and sportier alloy wheels.The GLC Electric gets a 39.1-inch MBUX Hyperscreen, which Mercedes-Benz says is its largest car display. It combines the driver’s instrument screen, central infotainment display and passenger screen into one unit.The system runs on fourth-generation MBUX software and includes an AI assistant. The SUV also retains physical controls on the steering wheel and centre console, while seating is provided for five occupants.The Mercedes-Benz GLC Electric is expected to cost between Rs 80 lakh and Rs 90 lakh (ex-showroom). It will compete with the BMW iX3 Long Wheelbase, which is expected to launch in India in 2027.

articles.body: GAYA: Smita Thackeray on Tuesday performed ‘pind daan’ and ‘shraddh’ rituals for her father-in-law and Shiv Sena founder Balasaheb Thackeray, as well as her father Madhukar Chitre, at the Vishnupad Temple here.Accompanied by her ‘acharya’ (priest), Thackeray performed ‘tarpan’, puja and other rituals amid Vedic chants. She was later blessed by Mohan Lal Barik, the Thackeray family’s priest in Gaya.Speaking after the ceremony, Thackeray said she had come to Gaya to pray for peace for Balasaheb Thackeray’s soul and seek forgiveness for any mistakes she may have committed towards him.She said she would try to follow the path shown by Balasaheb and work towards carrying forward Sanatan Dharma and his idea of a Hindu Rashtra.Thackeray said she was initially told that women do not perform ‘pind daan’, following which she sought clarification from acharyas. articles.title: In 2018, Elon Musk donated $480,350 for Flint school water filters; four years later, redesigned systems allowed students to drink from fountains again after years of relying on alternative supplies
articles.summary: For four years, students at Flint Community Schools relied on bottled and delivered water instead of drinking directly from school fountains.
articles.body: For four years, students at Flint Community Schools relied on bottled and delivered water instead of drinking directly from school fountains. That is now changing after new ultraviolet water filtration systems were installed and tested across the district. The project dates back to 2018, when Elon Musk donated $480,350 to help install water filtration stations following the Flint water crisis. The upgraded systems are designed to remove lead, bacteria and other metals from water before it reaches students. District officials say testing found no detectable lead or harmful bacteria after filtration, allowing the drinking stations to be used again.How the new water filters workA total of 130 filtration stations have been installed across Flint's 11 schools and administration building.The systems use three stages of filtration. Water first passes through an activated carbon filter designed to remove lead, copper and other particles. It then goes through an ultrafilter to remove most bacteria. Finally, ultraviolet light is used to kill remaining bacteria and viruses.Testing found lead levels before filtration varied by school. The highest average was 219 parts per billion (ppb) at Accelerated Learning Academy, while one test at Scott Elementary recorded 620 ppb. The US Environmental Protection Agency's recommended action level is 15 ppb.After filtration, tests found no detectable lead or harmful bacteria at the tested sites.Why did the project take four yearsThe stations were installed during the 2019-20 school year, but researchers found problems with the original filters during testing. The systems produced inconsistent results and were not certified to meet National Sanitation Foundation standards.Researchers later redesigned the systems and began testing new units in 2021.Superintendent Kevelin Jones said students can now drink from the hydration stations, but the district will continue providing bottled water for the rest of the school year as some families may still have concerns.The district also plans regular testing and filter replacements to monitor water quality.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1988, a Malibu developer and his wife bought land for $1.7 million, built a 17,700-square-foot mansion in 1991, and decades later listed the estate for $90 million
articles.summary: Discover the luxury of Venezia Pacifica, a custom-built mansion in Malibu's Point Dume, listed at $90 million. This iconic estate has Hollywood history and Mediterranean architecture, offering unparalleled oceanfront views.
articles.body: The luxury real estate market is seeing the entry of the largest cliffside residential property on Malibu’s Point Dume with a staggering price tag of $90 million according to the Wall Street Journal.The 1.16-acre property, beyond its architectural grandeur, comes with pop culture status, having served as a backdrop for Hollywood movies and series including The O.C. and Austin Powers: The Spy Who Shagged Me.Historically known as Venezia Pacifica, the custom-built mansion was completed in 1991, following the couple's 1988 land purchase, and is being offered for sale for the first time by its original owners. Property records cited by the paper show the property was acquired in 1988 by the late real estate developer Ken Harges and his wife, Lorelei Harges, for $1.7 million. Since the passing of Ken Harges in 2016, and his wife later on, their daughters Bonnie Furgurson and Wendy Geweke have decided to list the multi-million-dollar asset due to immense logistical challenges required in managing an estate of this magnitude. The couple's daughters said their parents wanted to leave inland life for the California coastline.Mediterranean architecture and interior design The primary residence incorporates a floor plan which is strongly evocative of classic Italian architecture, and inspiration from the couple’s historical travels through Italy has been etched directly into its structure. This sentiment for the region was echoed by their daughters, who wrote in a joint email cited by the Wall Street Journal: "Our mother was proudly 100% Italian," they said, "and together my parents drew inspiration from their many travels throughout Italy.The exterior is defined by classic columns, a signature terracotta-tiled roof, and an expansive circular motor court centered around a custom water fountain. Embracing 176 feet of direct bluff frontage, the estate’s perimeter overlooks the Pacific. Outside, the ocean facing grounds are landscaped with gardens and a sunken pavilion with columns to frame views of the immediate coastline.Inside, the architectural centerpiece is a massive, two-story central ballroom consisting of a sweeping glass curtain wall and an overhead barrel-vaulted glass ceiling. This expansive area is symmetrically flanked by a formal dining room on one side and a private library on the other. While the entry area showcases an artistic staircase alongside a custom glass elevator enclosed in decorative wrought ironwork. Throughout the estate’s nine bedrooms, the designs include coffered ceilings, structural columns, and intricate decorative millwork. Additionally, the primary bedroom suite is fitted with dual walk-in closets featuring motorized clothing carousels. Set apart from the living quarters is a 9,500-square-foot subterranean garage that can provide parking for 20 vehicles.The dynamics of the real estate market The listing of the Malibu mansion is making its debut in a coastal submarket that is highly active. According to listing agent Chris Cortazzo of Compass, the broader volatility across the greater Los Angeles luxury housing sector has done little to dissuade the micro-market of Malibu, which continues to remain energetic.Ultimately, the extensive acreage's pricing draws precedent from a comparable oceanfront property located nearby at Little Dume Beach, which previously sold for $80 million.However, the caveat is that since Venezia Pacifica was constructed before California's coastal and building regulations and height limits grew stricter, replicating a compound of this specific scale and blufftop proximity would be difficult under current zoning parameters. This tension between regulation and property value is not unique to Malibu. A UCSB study found that properties within California’s regulated coastal zone were valued 18% to 25% higherthan comparable properties outside it. Researchers attribute the premium partly to regulations that protect ocean views and limit coastal development.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2000, a Colorado man gave up money to leave debt and financial motives behind; 12 years later, he was still surviving through foraging, gifts and discarded goods
articles.summary: Explore the intriguing story of Daniel Suelo, who abandoned money in 2000 to live a life of foraging and generosity for over a decade. Discover how his unique lifestyle challenges societal norms about money and self-sufficiency.
articles.body: Daniel Shellabarger, who later became known as Daniel Suelo, decided to live without money in autumn 2000 after leaving his last thirty dollars in a phone booth at a truck stop in Pennsylvania, according to an account by Clay Bonnyman Evans published in The Coloradan. Mark Sundeen’s book The Man Who Quit Money, published in 2012, gave an account of Suelo’s way of life in the vicinity of Moab, Utah, where Suelo lived in a cave and gathered wild foods, as well as collected leftover food. In a blog post reproduced by Peace Corps Online, Suelo described money as a stand-in for the past as debt and the future as credit, never the present. The man had led a moneyless life, which is different from total self-reliance, since Suelo would accept any freely donated gifts and rejected any money or bartering system. This article looks at Suelo's lifestyle alongside two other sources: a 2006 psychology study on money and a federal report on food waste.University of Colorado degree and Peace Corps service in EcuadorSuelo's background appeared ordinary. Peace Corps Online, in a document reprinted in 2009, listed Suelo as a former Peace Corps volunteer in Ecuador who had earned an anthropology degree at the University of Colorado and worked as a lab technician. Furthermore, it is mentioned that he was 48 years old and lived in a cave around one hour away from Moab. The Coloradan’s account, as preserved by Clay Bonnyman Evans, placed him in the class of 1984. The Deseret News reported that he had been depressed for about 10 years before his 2000 decision.Twelve years of foraging and scavenging, 2000 to 2012Sundeen’s version, as quoted in the blog Citydesert, depicts the 12 years of living without money in which Suelo lived on wild edibles, scavenged food, some roadkill and gifts. An Associated Press profile of Suelo, published in the Summit Daily in 2009, provides additional details. Suelo went through Moab's garbage once a week and found more than enough for himself. Suelo assured the reporter that he never got sick because of the scavenged food.He rejected barter because he saw it as a form of money, the Deseret News reported. In an interview on Becoming Minimalist, he disagreed with the intro calling him boastful for avoiding food stamps and any other government assistance since it might imply that he considers himself superior to those who need such help. Gordon Stevenson, who directed a film about Suelo, talked to AP about the contradiction between Suelo's way of life and his reliance on people who use money. The Coloradan reported in 2013 that he had lived in a cave outside Moab for 13 years. Peace Corps Online's account of his 2000 hitchhike shows he did not stay in one place. In a 2021 profile, Utah Stories reported that he had made a home near Moab during the 1990s, before he gave up money.Vohs, Mead and Goode's nine money experiments, 2006In The Psychological Consequences of Money, published in Science, Kathleen Vohs, Nicole Mead and Miranda Goode reported nine experiments. The 2006 experiments suggested that money primes a more self-reliant orientation, making people less dependent on others, which offers background on how life without money differs from ordinary financial life. Moreover, they preferred to engage in solitary play, solitary work, and sit themselves at a greater distance from an unfamiliar individual compared to people exposed to neutral terms.USDA food waste estimates for 2010: 133 billion pounds, 31 percentThe food recovered by Suelo fits into the national pattern, which is well-established. USDA's Economic Research Service published a paper titled "The Estimated Amount, Value, and Calories of Postharvest Food Losses at the Retail and Consumer Levels in the United States." According to the statistics provided there, 133 billion pounds, out of 430 billion pounds of food available for consumption, were wasted in 2010, which is 31% of the available food, retail value of which was estimated at $161.6 billion. According to the estimates provided by the agency, retailers wasted 43 billion pounds of food, which is 10% of the available amount, and consumers wasted 90 billion pounds, which is 21%. The amount of wasted calories amounted to 387 billion per day, and meat, poultry and fish accounted for 30% of the total value lost.The agency reported that there was an average loss of 1,249 calories per person per day. Meat, poultry, and fish constituted 30 percent of the food wasted in terms of value, amounting to $48 billion. Reasons for wastage at the retail level included broken equipment like malfunctioning cold storage, ordering more than required and discarding damaged produce. This is shown by Suelo’s experience of the visible effect of food wastage; however, there are many other kinds of wastage included in the above statistics that cannot be recovered from trash.Suelo's return to financial society, 2015 to 2021Utah Stories reported in 2021 that Suelo's moneyless period lasted about 15 years, from 2000 until he returned to financial society in 2015 to care for his parents. A 2021 profile by Utah Stories described him as living in Colorado with his mother. articles.title: In 2011, Gary Sinise launched his foundation to support military families; by November 2025, it had dedicated its 100th mortgage-free adapted smart home, giving wounded veteran Joe Bowser a new start
articles.summary: For nearly two decades, wounded Army veteran Joe Bowser had turned down an offer that could have made everyday life much easier for him.
articles.body: For nearly two decades, wounded Army veteran Joe Bowser had turned down an offer that could have made everyday life much easier for him. That changed in November 2025, when the Gary Sinise Foundation dedicated its 100th mortgage-free, specially adapted smart home to him. According to the Gary Sinise Foundation’s own 2025 year-end campaign page, the milestone home was built around Bowser’s mobility needs, giving him and his wife, Michele, a safer and more accessible place to live. The milestone marked a major moment in the foundation’s work to provide specially adapted homes for severely wounded veterans.The injury that changed Joe Bowser’s lifeBowser’s story goes back to his military service in Iraq. He had served in the Army and later returned to the reserves following the September 11 attacks. In 2004, he was deployed to Iraq, where a rocket attack in April that year left him with serious injuries to his right leg. Doctors initially tried to save the leg, but after several operations, amputation eventually became necessary. Adjusting to life after such a severe injury was not easy, but Bowser found a way to reconnect with something he enjoyed: ice hockey.He later took part in hockey programmes for veterans with service-related injuries. For Bowser, the sport offered more than a chance to play. It helped him regain a sense of normality and reconnect with an activity he enjoyed before his injury. It was in 2006 that he met Sinise, beginning a friendship that would continue for years.Why he kept saying no to a new homeThe offer of a specially adapted home did not immediately appeal to Bowser. In fact, he spent years turning it down. The Gary Sinise Foundation had considered Bowser for its R.I.S.E. programme, which provides custom-built homes for wounded veterans. In an interview with PEOPLE, Sinise said Bowser repeatedly suggested that another veteran should receive the opportunity instead. Sinise told PEOPLE that Bowser was among those veterans who did not necessarily believe their injuries were severe enough to warrant a specially built home. Eventually, however, Bowser agreed.The decision came as the limitations of his existing home became harder to ignore. His previous house in West Virginia was built in 1839 and had narrow hallways and doorways that were difficult to navigate in a wheelchair. The second floor had also become increasingly challenging and unsafe for Bowser. He sometimes uses a wheelchair when he cannot use his prosthetic leg, making the layout of the old house particularly difficult.A home built around the way he livesThe new Tennessee house was designed with those everyday challenges in mind. According to PEOPLE, the approximately 2,991-square-foot, three-bedroom, single-storey ranch near Fort Campbell was built so that Bowser could move throughout the home without having to deal with stairs. The design includes five-foot-wide hallways, lower cabinets that can be reached from a wheelchair and an accessible shower fitted with a heated bench. These may seem like small details, but for someone navigating a home with a prosthetic leg or wheelchair, they can change how easily everyday activities are managed.The idea behind the foundation's specially adapted homes is not simply to provide a veteran with a house. The homes are designed around the individual needs of the person who will live there, with accessibility and independence built into the design. For Bowser, that means being able to move around his home more easily and safely.A milestone for the Gary Sinise FoundationBowser’s house also marked an important moment for the Gary Sinise Foundation. The organisation dedicated its 100th mortgage-free adapted smart home to him in November 2025. Its campaign page describes the homes as specially designed for severely wounded veterans, with accessibility features intended to help recipients regain independence in their daily lives.The house also gives Bowser and Michele more room to spend time with their family. The couple have 10 grandchildren, and the new home provides a setting where family gatherings can happen without the accessibility barriers they faced in their previous house. For the foundation, reaching 100 homes represents more than a numerical milestone. Each project involves creating a home around the specific needs of a veteran whose life has been affected by a serious service-related injury.A friendship that became part of the storyBowser’s connection with Sinise has also become deeply personal over the years. According to PEOPLE, the two men became even closer after each experienced the loss of a son to cancer. Bowser’s son Justin died in November 2023, while Sinise’s son Mac died in January 2024. Sinise launched the Gary Sinise Foundation in 2011 to support service members, veterans, first responders and their families. His interest in supporting veterans was also influenced by his experience playing Lieutenant Dan in Forrest Gump and his desire to help veterans after their service.For Bowser, the new home provides a single-storey layout and accessibility features designed around his mobility needs, while giving him, Michele and their family more room to spend time together.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Save Democracy March' announced: INDIA bloc projects unity amid SIR row, targets PM Modi, Amit Shah
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc on Wednesday announced a series of nationwide protests against the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR)
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc on Wednesday announced a series of nationwide protests against the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, seeking to project opposition unity amid the ongoing row over voter rolls.Addressing a press conference after the INDIA bloc meeting, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the alliance would hold district-level “Save Democracy” marches and demonstrations outside district magistrate offices from October 2 to 8.“From October 2 to 8, we will hold district-level 'Save Democracy' marches and stage demonstrations outside the offices of every district magistrate. We will also make people aware of why we are undertaking this campaign,” Kharge said.He said all opposition MPs would march to the Election Commission on October 6. Kharge said the opposition had initially planned to hold the march on Wednesday but decided to organise it later with greater participation.“On October 6, all opposition MPs will march to the Election Commission. We wanted to go today itself, but we decided to call the MPs again and organise the protest properly, so we have fixed October 6 for the march,” he said.Kharge added that Rajya Sabha members and MPs from all parties, as well as those who wanted to “protect democracy in the country”, would be invited to join the march.The alliance also plans to seek an appointment with President Droupadi Murmu in the second week of October. Leaders of the opposition will submit a representation outlining what Kharge described as the difficulties they were facing and the constitutional issues involved.A fourth phase of the campaign will comprise five major rallies, with their dates and venues to be announced later.The INDIA bloc meeting also saw Kharge reiterate his criticism of the Election Commission and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He alleged that the poll panel was being influenced by the government and said the parties had agreed to fight the issue together.“From October 2 to 8, we will hold district-level 'Save Democracy' marches and stage demonstrations outside the offices of every District Magistrate. We will also make people aware of why we are undertaking this campaign,” Kharge said.Addressing the briefing, ex-Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee lashed out at the CEC and call on him to resign."He (CEC Gyanesh Kumar) must resign immediately. Let us save the democracy and make the security of the people, the voting rights... It is our constitutional rights. It is our obligation to the people. If people are not voting, if their voting are been looted and cheated, then where the country will go? So, our request... it our demand. Our forceful demand," the former Bengal CM said.The opposition has demanded a rollback of the SIR exercise, greater transparency in electoral rolls and safeguards against the exclusion of eligible voters. Kharge also called for the use of pre-SIR electoral rolls for future elections and sought prior notice, reasons and an effective appeal mechanism before legitimate voters are removed.The meeting was attended by representatives of Congress, SP, AITC, NCP(SP), SS (UBT), RJD, CPM, CPI, JKNC, JKPDP, JMM, CPI-ML, IUML, KC(M), MDMK, VCK, RSP, KC(J) and AIFB.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Boeing to build US Navy’s sixth-gen F/A-XX fighter as India steps up its own plans
articles.summary: The US Navy has formally selected Boeing to build its next carrier-based fighter under the F/A-XX programme, ending a competition that had run for years
articles.body: The US Navy has formally selected Boeing to build its next carrier-based fighter under the F/A-XX programme, ending a competition that had run for years and putting the manufacturer back at the centre of America's future airpower plans. Boeing released a fresh render of the winning design alongside the announcement, offering the clearest look yet at what the Navy's sixth-generation jet is expected to look like, a tailless, sharply blended airframe built around all-aspect stealth shaping, reflecting the same design language now emerging across next-generation fighter programmes worldwide. Earlier last year, US President Donald Trump had unveiled the US Air Force's sixth-generation project, known as the F-47 at the Oval Office.That global race is exactly where India is now trying to find its footing. The defence ministry has confirmed that the country is simultaneously engaging with both of the world's leading sixth-generation fighter projects, the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP) of the UK, Japan and Italy, and the Future Combat Air System (FCAS), now a largely French-led effort after Germany's exit. Defence minister Rajnath Singh has said India is planning to produce both fifth and sixth generation fighters domestically. FCAS, with France now firmly in the driving seat and Spain still on board, is expected to take its first flight around 2028-29, roughly coinciding with the planned first flight of India's own fifth-generation Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft, in a parallel timeline.The Franco-German split itself has worked in India's favour. Disagreements over aircraft carrier operability and nuclear delivery capabilities pushed Germany out of FCAS, but India, unlike Germany, already possesses both capabilities, making its operational doctrine a closer match for French requirements. The defence ministry told the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Defence earlier this month that it has initiated concerted efforts to co-join the French-led FCAS programme.The stakes behind this positioning are considerable. Sixth-generation fighters are expected to bring all-aspect stealth shaping, digital-first engineering, variable-cycle engines, gallium nitride-powered radars and directed-energy weapons, layered with artificial intelligence, cyber warfare tools and manned-unmanned teaming alongside loyal wingman drones. Boeing's F/A-XX win joins an increasingly crowded field, sitting alongside the US Air Force's F-47 under the Next Generation Air Dominance project, while China is already flight-testing its own J-36 and J-50 prototypes. For India, engaging both GCAP and FCAS is less about picking a side and more about ensuring it has a seat at the table as the rules of future aerial combat are being written.

articles.title: An Illinois woman allegedly concealed her mother’s body in a garage freezer for two years, assumed her identity and continued collecting Social Security and food benefits; prosecutors put the intended loss at $21,402
articles.summary: A Chicago case involving an elderly woman’s death has taken a new turn in federal court, with prosecutors alleging that her daughter concealed her
articles.body: A Chicago case involving an elderly woman’s death has taken a new turn in federal court, with prosecutors alleging that her daughter concealed her mother’s body in a garage freezer for nearly two years while continuing to collect government benefits in her name. According to the Chicago Tribune, Eva Bratcher, 72, has been indicted in U.S. District Court on two fraud counts tied to more than $20,000 in Social Security and food assistance benefits that prosecutors say were obtained after her mother’s death in 2021. The indictment was initially filed under seal in August and was announced Tuesday by the U.S. Department of Justice as part of a nationwide enforcement effort targeting Social Security fraud.Body allegedly kept in freezerThe report states that according to federal prosecutors, Bratcher’s 96-year-old mother, Regina Michalski, died on March 4, 2021, at the Chicago home the two women shared. Authorities allege that about a week later, Bratcher purchased a new freezer and placed her mother’s body inside it. Investigators later found the freezer receipt at the residence. The body remained undiscovered until January 2023, when a relative became suspicious and contacted Chicago police. An autopsy was subsequently conducted, although the results were inconclusive.The discovery triggered a separate criminal case in Cook County, where Bratcher was charged with concealing a death or moving a body and possessing a fraudulent identification document.Alleged identity theftThe report also states that the federal prosecutors now allege that the concealment was accompanied by a broader effort to continue accessing benefits intended for Michalski. The indictment alleges that Bratcher assumed her mother’s identity and continued receiving Social Security benefits after her death. Prosecutors also accuse her of using her mother’s Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits and an alternative Social Security number to obtain additional SNAP assistance for which she was allegedly not eligible. The intended loss in the federal case is listed at $21,402.Authorities also allege that Bratcher possessed at least one identification card bearing her mother’s name but Bratcher’s photograph when she was arrested in connection with the earlier case, the online report adds.Earlier case ended in guilty pleaThe federal charges follow a state prosecution stemming from the discovery of Michalski’s body. According to court records, Bratcher had recorded her mother’s death on a calendar at the home. She later pleaded guilty in August 2023 to concealing her mother’s death and received a sentence of 213 days in jail, with credit for time already served.Bratcher, a U.S. Army veteran who was born in Poland, also had previous convictions for forgery, violating an order of protection and domestic battery, according to court records. The new federal indictment focuses specifically on the alleged theft of government benefits and identity-related fraud rather than the concealment of the body itself.Federal fraud crackdownThe charges were announced as part of a broader Justice Department initiative focused on fraud involving Social Security programs. Federal authorities have increasingly targeted cases in which benefits continue to be collected after recipients die or are obtained through the use of another person's identity. Bratcher is scheduled to make her first appearance in federal court at the Dirksen U.S. Courthouse in Chicago. Court records did not list an attorney for her at the time the charges were announced. The federal indictment contains allegations, and Bratcher is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.Images Courtesy: Chicago Tribune and istockYou use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient.
